page: Vultr vcg-l40s-32c-375g-96vram is a Cloud GPU server configured with 32 vCPUs and 32 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 6448H processor operating at 2.0 GHz. The system features an x86_64 architecture with a shared CPU allocation and no hyperthreading. It is equipped with 375.0 GB of system memory, yielding 11.72 GB per core. For acceleration, the server bundles two NVIDIA L40S GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing a total of 96 GB of VRAM. Local storage consists of a 2200 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate strong performance across multiple domains. Multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng is rated strong at 62892.75, and the Passmark CPU score reaches 64768.69. The server demonstrates top-tier capabilities in LLM inference, processing 13643.47 tokens per second for prompts and generating 348.06 tokens per second on a small 135M model, alongside 6275.36 tokens per second for prompts on a medium 7B model. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression is also top-tier at 15.2 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is strong for read operations, reaching 4985.78 GB/sec for cached small blocks, though large block write bandwidth is average at 88.2 GB/sec.

This server offers high resource density by combining substantial system memory and dual enterprise GPUs with local NVMe storage, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for specialized parallel computing. However, the shared CPU allocation represents a potential tradeoff for workloads requiring dedicated, non-shared host CPU cycles. Given its hardware profile and top-tier LLM inference benchmarks, this instance is highly suited for machine learning inference, data science, database operations, and high-throughput web serving.
description: Vultr vcg-l40s-32c-375g-96vram is a Cloud GPU server designed for parallel computing and memory-intensive workloads. It features 32 vCPUs on an Intel Xeon 6448H processor, 375.0 GB of RAM, and a 2200 GB NVMe SSD. The server is equipped with two NVIDIA L40S GPUs from the Ada Lovelace architecture, delivering 96 GB of total VRAM. Benchmarks show top-tier performance in LLM inference, with prompt processing speeds of 6275.36 tokens per second on a 7B model, and strong multi-core CPU capabilities. While the shared CPU allocation is a potential tradeoff, the high GPU-to-memory density provides qualitative cost efficiency for complex workloads. This server is optimized for machine learning inference, data science, database operations, and high-throughput web serving.
